points.description: Method: Correct application of circuit analysis principles (ideal op-amp behavior, KCL/KVL, and current directions).
points.partial_credit: Deductions: -1 for each error (method_opamp_inputs, method_unjustified_vp_vm, method_no_kcl_kvl_structure, method_wrong_reference). Max deduction 4.

points.description: Equations: Correct formation of KCL/KVL and Ohm's law relationships.
points.partial_credit: Deductions: -3 for eq_kcl_node_signs, -3 for eq_ohms_wrong_element, -2 for eq_kvl_input_loop_error. Max deduction 8.

points.description: Calculation: Correct arithmetic, algebra, and sign handling.
points.partial_credit: Deductions: -2 for each error (calc_numeric_error, calc_unit_scale_error, calc_inconsistency). Max deduction 8.

points.description: Units: Correct and consistent use of units throughout the solution.
points.partial_credit: Deductions: -1 for each error (unit_missing_final, unit_incorrect_type, unit_inconsistent). Max deduction 3.

points.description: Completeness: Inclusion of all required results (vo and io) and clear supporting work.
points.partial_credit: Deductions: -5 for nc_missing_vo_or_io, -3 for nc_sparse_work, -2 for nc_missing_definitions. Max deduction 10.

rubric.notes: The student starts with 100 marks. Deduct marks for each specific error identified in the rubric categories. Ensure that deductions do not exceed the maximum allowed for each category.
rubric.answer_key: The solution requires applying KCL at the inverting node and KVL around the input loop, assuming ideal op-amp characteristics (v+ = v- = 0V). Solving the resulting system of equations yields the final values for vo and io.
